edges.description: Enhanced autoactivation or loss of the trypsin inactivation site raises active trypsin within the pancreas.
Excess active trypsin triggers the intracellular protease cascade that digests acinar tissue.
Repeated autodigestive injury produces recurrent acute pancreatitis attacks.
Repeated acinar injury drives fibrosis and irreversible chronic pancreatitis.
Acute pancreatitis attacks present with abdominal pain.
Recurrent acute attacks progress to chronic pancreatitis.
Advancing chronic pancreatitis destroys acinar tissue, producing exocrine insufficiency.
Islet loss in advancing chronic pancreatitis produces pancreatogenic diabetes.
Chronic pancreatic inflammation markedly raises pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma risk.
Loss of exocrine pancreatic lipase and digestive enzyme secretion causes fat maldigestion and steatorrhea.
Tobacco use accelerates progression to chronic pancreatitis and raises cancer risk.
Alcohol precipitates and aggravates pancreatitis attacks.
